items.title: CJI Surya Kant presents Madhava Menon memorial award to Attorney General R Venkataramani
items.summary: Attorney General or India R Venkataramani was conferred with the Madhava Menon Memorial Award on Saturday. The award, instituted in the memory of the eminent legal educationist Dr. NR Madhava Menon, was presented by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant in Kochi. The event was organised by the Bar Council of Kerala and the Bar Council of Kerala Advocates Academy for Continuing Legal Education Trust. In his address, the CJI recalled the contributions of Professor Menon. CJI Kant said Professor Menon's efforts to establish institutions such as the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru, the West Bengal National University of Juridicial Sciences, Kolkata and the National Judicial Academy, Bhopal, were guided by a common vision. " Each bearing the unmistakable imprint of one conviction: that law, when taught rightly, is an instrument of social transformation, and not merely a licence to practise a trade, " the CJI said. CJI Kant added that Professor Menon's approach to legal education placed the needs of disadvantaged communities at the centre of legal training. " He gave it life not through legislation, but through education, through curricula and legal aid clinics that placed the poor and the marginalised at the very centre of legal training, rather than leaving them at its periphery, " he said. Prof (Dr) NR Madhavan Menon The CJI also reflected on the relationship between Professor Menon and Attorney General Venkataramani, who had studied under him at Government Law College, Pondicherry. He said that AG Venkataramani joined the college in 1974, the same year when Professor Menon became its principal, marking the beginning of a lifelong relationship between the teacher and a student. " It is a teacher’s vision finding vindication in a student’s achievement. A lineage of learning that runs, unbroken, from a small college in Pondicherry to the highest office of legal counsel in the land, " the CJI added. CJI Surya Kant He praised AG Venkataramani's contributions to the legal profession for nearly five decades and said that his measured approach, commitment to principles and unfailing courtesy were qualities developed through years of learning as well as experience. Presenting the award to AG Venkataramani was particularly meaningful because his achievements reflected the values that Professor Menon had sought to instil in his students. items.title: Transparency on trial: Mapping courts’ compliance with the RTI Act
items.summary: The effectiveness of the Right to Information (RTI) regime has, in recent years, come under a cloud of uncertainty with commentators pointing at a progressive weakening of RTI mechanisms. Among the concerns are onerous delays in appointments of information commissioners and other officials, rising backlogs and arbitrary rejections of requests by public authorities . The amendment effected to Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act by the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 further exacerbated these concerns as it empowered public authorities to deny information if it qualified as ‘personal information’, without requiring it to be weighed against public interest. While the High Courts and the Supreme Court often find themselves adjudicating upon the failure of government ministries and departments to comply with the RTI Act, the courts themselves are guilty of not adhering to the principles of the Act. The 2024-25 Annual Report of the Central Information Commission (CIC) reveals that among all public authorities in the country, the Delhi High Court has the highest rate of rejection of RTI applications followed by the Supreme Court. More often than not, courts withhold information that relates to institutional probity and conduct of judicial personnel -information that is crucial for affixing accountability. Hence, it is imperative to analyse these acts of omission and commission. Weaponising exemptions Firstly, courts have been thwarting RTI queries seeking clarity on judicial examinations, disciplinary conduct of judges and internal administrative affairs, by taking the cover of the exemptions laid out under Section 8 of the Act, even where the information demanded lies beyond the ambit of the exemptions. Particularly, Section 8(1)(j) is often invoked by High Courts, thus lending credence to the apprehensions being expressed over the DPDP amendment. This year, the Chhattisgarh High Court cited the provision to overrule a direction issued by the State Information Commission (SIC), refusing to disclose details of the complaints and inquiries against three judicial officers. In a similar case, the Delhi High Court in August last year had refused to disclose complaints details, again primarily invoking Section 8(1)(j). items.title: Logical discrepancy but illogical interim orders?
items.summary: The Supreme Court orally said on October 28 that it has not decided on the validity of the 'logical discrepancy' parameter used by the Election Commission of India (ECI) to weed out electors in its special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in various States. While the Court upheld the validity of the SIR exercise in Bihar , it has now said that the logical discrepancy issue was not decided in that matter. The Court had earlier also permitted the ECI to employ 'logical discrepancy' in West Bengal prior to the assembly polls in the State. However, it has now clarified that the same was only an interim measure and not a final decision. The remarks were made by a Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana after the ECI counsel argued that the apex court had examined every step of SIR and upheld it. "Ever since the SIR process was initiated, Your Lordships have been seized of the matter and have examined every step. Your Lordships may recall what happened in Bihar," the counsel said. "Bihar is not a final determination of every question arising in these proceedings. In Bihar, the Election Commission had not initially undertaken logical discrepancy as a category. We permitted it as an interim arrangement in West Bengal. We have not finally adjudicated upon the legality of the logical discrepancy exercise," Justice Bagchi remarked. The Supreme Court's handling of the West Bengal SIR case warrants attention in this context. Various petitions, including one filed by then Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, came up before the Supreme Court earlier this year seeking a stay on SIR in the State just before the assembly elections. Banerjee contended that the SIR process should not be rushed and should be completed only after following all due procedure. She flagged the immediate and irreversible threat of mass disenfranchisement of eligible voters in the upcoming state assembly elections through a flawed SIR process. Thus, she sought a direction that the polls be conducted based on the existing rolls prepared last year. items.title: Madras High Court forms judicial panel to take over Chidambaram Nataraja Temple administration
items.summary: The Madras High Court has constituted a five-member board of management headed by two retired High Court judges to take over the administration of the Chidambaram Nataraja Temple [Sabanayagar Temple Vs State of TN]. A Division Bench of Justices G Jayachandran and E Manoharan passed the order after finding maladministration, damage to heritage structures and failure to properly account for temple properties. The Court held that judicial intervention was necessary to address the irregularities in the management of the temple by the Podhu Dikshitars, a religious denomination constitutionally entitled to administer its affairs. Interestingly, the order was passed on a petition filed by Podhu Dikshitars themselves who moved the Court taking objection to a government order permitting devotees to climb atop a Mandapam for the darshan of the temple deity. " Therefore, we constitute a Board of Management consisting of domain experts, who will take over the administration, till the ill is cured, " the Court said. Justice G Jayachandran and Justice E Manoharan The Board will be chaired by retired High Court Justice V Bharathidasan, with retired Justice R Suresh Kumar as co-chairman. Retired IAS officer C Rajendran, the Secretary of the Podhu Dikshitars and the Secretary of the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department will be its other members. The October 30 judgment came on petitions challenging a 2022 Tamil Nadu government order permitting devotees to climb the Kanagasabai Mandapam for darshan of Lord Nataraja. The Podhu Dikshitars (petitioners) argued that the order interfered with their constitutional right under Article 26 to administer the temple's religious affairs. They relied on the Supreme Court's 2014 judgment in Dr. Subramanian Swamy v. State of Tamil Nadu, which had protected their denominational rights. However, the High Court rejected the contention that the government order constituted a colourable exercise of executive power intended to override those rights. The Bench also examined allegations of unauthorised construction, damage to ancient sculptures and murals, encroachment of temple properties and irregularities in financial accounts. items.title: Mercedes crash: What action taken against online posts revealing minor accused's identity? Kerala Court to Police
items.summary: A sessions court in Kerala on Saturday criticised the police for not acting against social media posts revealing the identity of the minor teenager accused of driving a Mercedes-Benz car under the influence of alcohol and killing a scooterist. The 17-year-old accused, the son of an additional district judge, was driving a Mercedes-Benz car when he hit a two-wheeler in Kochi's Cheranalloor in the early hours of October 25, killing the scooterist - one, Jayabalakrishnan. Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Judge Kavitha Gangadharan today heard pleas to cancel the bail granted on October 26 to the teenager. During the hearing, the court took exception to the continued circulation of social media posts that revealed the teenager's identity. Notably, Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, prohibits the disclosure of the identity of a child in conflict with law (CCL), except with the permission of the competent authority. "I will pass an order - direct the cyber police to take down every social media account and post that is revealing the identity of the CCL. This is a sessions court and a children's court. Why does the cyber police exist? How can this be allowed?" the judge asked today. The court proceeded to order the police to submit a report on the action taken against such posts. "The investigating officer is directed to produce the case diary and appear before the court on November 2. The cyber police shall submit a report on the action taken regarding the publication of the identity of the child in conflict with law (CCL) by various social media accounts and platforms," it ordered. The matter is listed next on Monday, November 2. items.title: Kashmir law student lands Trilegal internship after his case management platform wins at hackathon
items.summary: Hammad Altaf Hafiz , a third-year B.A.LL.B. student at the University of Kashmir, has won the Vibecode Law Vibeathon with CourtSync , a case management platform he built for lawyers. CourtSync took first place at competition organised by Indian LegalTech Network and sponsored by Trilegal. Hafiz has received ₹75,000 as prize money and an internship at Trilegal. Hafiz is an intern at M/S Malik & Muazzam Law Chambers in Srinagar where the case diary and the day’s cause list were kept by hand. The idea for CourtSync came after discussions with his seniors there. Hafiz has no coding background and built the platform with AI tools by describing what a chamber needs in plain language and refining it step by step. His seniors let him build against live cases and the chamber now uses CourtSync in everyday practice. CourtSync lets users export their cases from the eCourts app and import all High Court and district court cases. Cases can be filtered by forum, assigned lawyer, date and client. A calendar shows every date. Lawyers get a notification at 9 AM listing the day’s cases, while each associate gets a separate alert with only their assigned cases. At 6 PM, everyone gets the next day’s list. On a hearing day, CourtSync picks up the cases a lawyer has listed. The lawyer selects the ones to follow on the court’s digital display board and the phone buzzes when a case is three away, two away, next and called. Every night, it once again checks each case on the court’s website and updates the next date, stage and court. A report shows what changed and what could not be checked. Each morning, it reads the published cause lists of High Courts, district courts, tribunals and consumer commissions, matches them to the firm’s cases and produces one list to download or print. Its newest feature checks court websites nightly for new orders, downloads the PDF, saves it with the case and notifies the lawyers on that case. Earlier orders stay on the case page.

items.title: Activists allege campaign to silence boys who accused Mangaluru Catholic priest of sex abuse
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The families of the five Mangaluru boys who accused their parish priest Cyprian Pinto of sexual abuse are allegedly under tremendous pressure to not pursue the case. According to community members, Cyprian’s supporters have tried to coerce the families, and certain clergy members have attempted to subtly direct blame at the survivors, accusing the five boys of making “false allegations” and “dividing” the church. Father Cyprian Pinto, who was the parish priest at St Vincent Ferrer Church in Valencia, Mangaluru, faces accusations of sexually assaulting at least five boys. Following a complaint by one boy, he was booked under sections 8 and 10 (sexual assault) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and section 75(2) (sexual harassment) of the BNS. He was arrested on October 17 and obtained bail on October 29. Activists and community members have alleged a systemic attempt to shield Cyprian even before the FIR was filed on October 15. Wilfy (name changed), a member of St Vincent, was part of a delegation of community members who met Police Commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy on October 30 and filed a complaint accusing the church’s vice president, Ronald Rodrigues, of intimidating the boys and their families. “I have been told that the vice president has intimidated the children’s parents. He has scared them by saying that they will be called repeatedly by the police, that they’ll have to go to court, that their children’s studies will be affected, that their children’s identities will be exposed in the media …” Wilfy alleged to TNM. “Knowing very well that the boy’s family is not well off, Ronald Rodrigues called the boy’s mother on October 15 and pressured her not to file the complaint,” the complaint reads. Wilfy was referring to the boy whose complaint led to an FIR being filed on the same day. Misusing the pulpit? Mangaluru-based activist Robert Rosario also alleged that attempts are being made to turn the community’s opinion against the survivors and that a section of priests have tried to meet the mother of the boy who filed the complaint. Robert has emailed the Mangalore Bishop regarding these developments. items.title: Andhra man unleashes savage chainsaw attack on teen girl and friend inside classroom, arrested
items.summary: A 21-year-old man has been arrested for the horrific power chainsaw attack on a 14-year-old student in Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur district. The accused, identified as Hemanth, was arrested near Dharmavaram Railway station on Saturday, October 31, in the afternoon, a few hours after he attacked a girl’s face, neck and torso with a power chainsaw in Raptadu mandal. The tenth-grade student, identified as Gopika, was attacked by Hemanth inside a Zilla Parishad High School classroom in Raptadu as class was in session. The victim suffered critical injuries to her head, neck and back, while her classmate, Lakshmi, who tried to intervene, was also injured in the process. A horrified Lakshmi told the media, "It happened around 10.30 am. He turned on the chainsaw and entered the classroom. He attacked [Gopika] in front of the teacher. Then he attacked me in the leg. She collapsed right there. All the students went out of the classroom. He took the chainsaw and escaped on his bike. The teacher also saw the chainsaw and got scared. He came alone. It was the first time I saw him. It all happened in around 5 minutes.” According to reports, Hemanth had proposed to her, but she had rejected his proposal. The rejection is suspected to be the motive for Hemanth’s attack. Speaking to local media, a teacher who was in the class at the time of the attack said that she was horrified. "I was teaching maths, and I heard the chainsaw. He walked into the class, and at that point I didn't know what to make of it. Then he went straight to the students and before we knew it, he attacked her. I just froze and stood against the wall. Children started running about," she said amid tears adding that he was the sole attacker. The school management reportedly noticed Hemanth on the school premises with the chainsaw, but mistook him for a construction worker. Following the attack, Hemanth fled the school. The victim and her classmate were shifted to the Anantapur government general hospital for emergency care. “She (Gopika) was brought here in an unconscious state. She has suffered severe injuries because of the nature of the weapon. A flap of one side of her face has completely come off. Muscles in her neck and back, paraspinal muscles, were cut.
